original_statement: The core never interprets contribution bytes; drivers do. Rounds, serialization domain, membership model, and finality are driver-described, never hardcoded.
restatement: The core must stay generic across coordination protocols, treating contribution bytes as opaque and driving purely from driver-declared policy: (s1) the core's own routing behavior is unaffected by what contribution bytes actually contain; (s2) the core's round count, membership-model dispatch, and finality handling always match exactly what the driver's describe() returns, never a hardcoded default; (s3) swapping in a different driver requires no core code changes — the core adapts purely from describe().

restatement_clauses.text: The core's own routing behavior is unaffected by what contribution bytes actually contain — it never parses or interprets their content.
The core's round count, membership-model dispatch, and finality handling always match exactly what the driver's describe() returns, never a hardcoded default.
Swapping in a different driver (different round count, membership model, finality type) requires no core code changes — the core adapts purely from describe().

goal: The core treats contribution bytes as opaque and routes purely on what the driver's describe() reports — never on hardcoded assumptions or by inspecting the bytes itself.
